subject: Genetics
title: Identifying the Unknown Dead
description: A fast breakdown of Identifying the Unknown Dead for builders.

hook.text: In America, over 13,000 unidentified bodies sit in morgues and graves. Some have been nameless for decades.

buildup.text: NamUs, the national missing persons database, connects DNA from remains to families searching for loved ones.

discovery.text: Genetic genealogy now identifies Does—unidentified dead. The same technique that catches killers names victims.

twist.text: Some families learn their missing relative died decades ago, miles away. The answer is relief and heartbreak at once.

climax.text: Projects like the DNA Doe Project use volunteers and genealogy to name the nameless. Crowdsourced justice.

punchline.text: Everyone deserves a name. DNA gives it back.

quiz.question: How many unidentified bodies exist in the U.S.?
